THE DATA CENTER DOSSIERS.

THE DECISIONS.

[[facility-3301-hibbetts-road-data-center]] 3301 Hibbetts Road Data Center, a data center on the Texas register
An Austin building that housed Hewlett Packard, taken over by Core Scientific and leased to CoreWeave in the deal that put the two companies back together. The certification is named for the street address rather than for either company.
Capacity contracted to CoreWeave is 16 megawatts. Total potential revenue in the announcement is $100 million. Occupant of record is Coreweave, Inc. Operators of record is Core Scientific, Inc. / Coreweave Compute Acquisition Co. II. LLC / CCAC IV.II, LLC. Owner of record is None is listed. Location is Austin, Travis County.
The two companies had a history before this. Core Scientific hosted CoreWeave hardware from before the bankruptcy, stopped, and started again with this contract. The state writes one of the operators as Coreweave Compute Acquisition Co. II. LLC, with a full stop where the other rows use a comma. Entity resolution here strips punctuation for matching and publishes what the state wrote, so this row and its siblings resolve to one company and still read as filed.
What the record does not carry for this one. Acreage is not public. No owner of record is listed. Whether the sixteen megawatts is delivered or only contracted is not stated in the record. The building's total capacity, as against CoreWeave's share, is not public.

[[facility-bexar-1]] Bexar 1, a data center on the Texas register
An Amazon facility certified under an internal codename. Amazon is owner, occupant and operator of record, so the filing discloses no landlord, no developer and no location, and this codename appears in no public reporting.
Owner, occupant and operator of record is Amazon Data Services, Inc. holds 3 roles in the registry. What the name suggests is The name points at Bexar County.
Amazon files Texas projects under internal codenames rather than under its own brand. A state licensing filing for a San Antonio building carries the name Lavender Hill, and this registry carries a set of names that appear in no public reporting at all. For these facilities the Comptroller's list is the only public record that they exist.
What the record does not carry for this one. The county and address are not public. Capacity, square footage and acreage are not public. No filing or company release names this facility. This entry is deliberately thin and is a candidate for a county appraisal district pass.

[[facility-c1-bosque-i]] C1 Bosque I, a data center on the Texas register
One of two certifications on a Bosque County campus, and the state names Google as its occupant. Its operator entity is the same one that operates Google's Panhandle campus.
Occupant of record is Google, LLC. Owner of record is Bosque Parcel 2, LLC. Operator of record is Design, LLC. County is Bosque County, from the facility name.
Design, LLC also appears as an operator on the Meitner campus in the Panhandle, whose occupant is also Google. The same operator entity on two separate Google facilities is a pattern visible only by reading the registry across rows. CyrusOne is building a hyperscale campus in Bosque County beside a Calpine gas plant and has not named its tenant publicly. Whether these certifications cover that campus is not established by the sources read here, so no capacity or investment figure from it is published on this page.
What the record does not carry for this one. Capacity, square footage and acreage are not public for this certification. The street address is not public. Whether this is part of the CyrusOne Bosque County campus is not established. What distinguishes parcel one from parcel two is not stated in the record.

[[facility-c1-bosque-ii-llc]] C1 Bosque II LLC, a data center on the Texas register
The sibling certification to the other Bosque parcel, granted days later, and the state names a different hyperscaler as its occupant. Google on one parcel, Amazon on this one.
Occupant of record is Amazon Data Services, Inc. Owner of record is C1 Bosque II LLC. Operator of record is C1 Bosque II LLC. County is Bosque County, from the facility name.
Two certifications share the Bosque name and were granted days apart, and the occupants are different companies. Reading either row alone would give a reader one hyperscaler and no reason to suspect the other.
What the record does not carry for this one. Capacity, square footage and acreage are not public for this certification. The street address is not public. The relationship between this entity and the other Bosque parcel is not stated in the record. Whether this is part of the CyrusOne Bosque County campus is not established.

[[facility-c1-richardson-llc-data-center]] C1 Richardson LLC Data Center, a data center on the Texas register
A CoreWeave certification in the Dallas suburbs whose owner and operator are the same single purpose entity. Its name opens with a prefix that appears across this registry on buildings that share nothing else.
Owner of record is C1 Richardson LLC. Occupant of record is Coreweave, Inc. Operator of record is C1 Richardson LLC. Location is Richardson, Dallas County. Name prefix is C1.
One entity in two of the three roles, and the tenant in the third. That is the simplest shape a certification takes and it is worth naming, because most of the large rows here are nothing like it. The same prefix opens the Bosque rows and a Dallas Allen row in this registry, on buildings with different owners and different occupants. A prefix is not a parent company and reading it as one would merge unrelated filings.
What the record does not carry for this one. Capacity, square footage and acreage are not public. No announcement names this facility. Whether that prefix is a developer brand or a naming convention is not established.

[[facility-cedarvale-barslow-pyote-tx-data-center]] Cedarvale, Barslow/Pyote TX Data Center, a data center on the Texas register
A West Texas site that mined bitcoin and now hosts AI. Nscale leases the whole of it and is filling it with Nvidia hardware for Microsoft, and neither of those companies is named on this facility's row.
Site capacity leased to Nscale is 234 megawatts. Contracted revenue over the lease is $2 billion. Nvidia GB300 units to be deployed is 104,000 units. Stated expansion ambition for the site is 1.2 gigawatts. Further capacity Microsoft may take from late 2027 is 700 megawatts. Address is 3013 FM 516, Barstow, Texas. County is Ward County. Lease is Nscale triple net lease for 10 years. First certification, occupant Ionic Digital Mining LLC is The site certified for mining use. Second certification, occupant Nscale Ward County Borrower SPV, LLC is Re-certified for AI hosting. Certifications Microsoft holds in its own name elsewhere in Texas is 14 facilities.
The state spells the facility Barslow. The town is Barstow, and the address Ionic gives sits there. Published as the state published it, because a reader comparing this against the Comptroller's own list should find the same string. Microsoft is the customer behind the hardware going into this building and is not named on this row. It is not absent from the registry, though. Microsoft holds certifications of its own across San Antonio and Red Oak, so its absence here is not avoidance. At this site it is the occupant's customer rather than the occupant, and the certified occupant is a single purpose Nscale borrowing entity. Two certifications carry this facility name, an earlier one naming the mining occupant and a later one naming Nscale's borrowing entity. Both read as live. A registry row names who holds an exemption now rather than who held it when it was granted. So the pair is two live exemptions rather than a dated handover, and what the site became is established by the lease.
What the record does not carry for this one. Square footage and acreage are not public. Cooling design is not public. The split between the mining build and the AI retrofit is not public. Whether the expansion ambition has any executed contract behind it is not established.

[[facility-cipher-barber-lake-llc-data-center]] Cipher Barber Lake LLC Data Center, a data center on the Texas register
A former bitcoin mining site at Colorado City converted to AI hosting. Fluidstack leases the whole of it under agreements Google backstops, and the state certified Anthropic as qualifying occupant.
Critical IT load is 168 megawatts. Gross capacity is 244 megawatts. Surrounding land held for expansion is 587 acres. Total site expansion potential is 500 megawatts. Contracted revenue, initial term is $3 billion. Contracted revenue with both extensions is $7 billion. Google backstop of lease obligations is $1.4 billion. Google warrant stake, pro forma is 5.4 percent. Estimated project cost per critical IT megawatt, low is $9 million. Estimated project cost per critical IT megawatt, high is $11 million. Location is Colorado City, Texas. Initial colocation term is 10 years. Extension options is 2 options. Length of each extension option is 5 years. Expected delivery is September of 2026.
A later agreement that autumn took Fluidstack to the entire capacity of the site. Cipher Mining rebranded to Cipher Digital the following spring as its business moved from mining to hosting. Google received warrants alongside the backstop, so its exposure here is both as guarantor and as a shareholder in the landlord.
What the record does not carry for this one. Building square footage is not public. Cooling design is not public. Substation and interconnection detail is not public.

[[facility-cipher-black-pearl-llc-data-center]] Cipher Black Pearl LLC Data Center, a data center on the Texas register
Cipher's Winkler County site at Wink, leased to Amazon on the longest and largest single agreement in this batch.
Gross capacity is 300 megawatts. Critical IT load is 216 megawatts. Lease value is $5.5 billion. Amazon cost overrun threshold per IT megawatt is $9.5 million. Location is Wink, Winkler County. Initial Amazon lease term is 15 years. Amazon extension options is 3 options. Length of each Amazon extension option is 5 years. First certification, occupant Cipher Black Pearl LLC is Certified for the owner's own use. Second certification, occupant Amazon Data Services is Re-certified with a hyperscaler as occupant.
The agreement puts construction cost overruns above a stated threshold per megawatt on Amazon rather than on the landlord, which is unusual enough to be worth noting. This facility holds two rows in the state registry rather than one. The earlier carries Cipher itself as occupant and the later carries Amazon. Both are live certifications as read, so the pair shows two exemptions running under one facility name rather than a dated handover. The move from mining to hosting here is established by the Amazon lease, not by the rows.
What the record does not carry for this one. Square footage, acreage and cooling design are not public. Energization timeline is not public. Primary filing was not read directly for this entry, so the figures here carry trade press rung. Whether the two certifications cover the same building or separate phases is not stated. Whether the earlier certification still covers active mining is not public.

[[facility-dfw-10]] DFW 10, a data center on the Texas register
One building on DataBank's Red Oak campus south of Dallas, with Oracle as the certified occupant. Four of these were certified on the same day and Oracle is the occupant of record on every one.
Campus capacity is 480 megawatts. Campus area is 292 acres. Planned buildings on the campus is 8 buildings. Gross area per building is 425,000 square feet. Owner of record is DB Data Center Red Oak, LLC. Operator of record is Databank Holdings LTD. Occupant of record is Oracle America Cloud Services. Location is Red Oak, south of Dallas. This building is Not to be confused with the CyrusOne building of the same designation in Bosque County. This one is DataBank's, at Red Oak, and the registry names its owner and operator.
DataBank has said Oracle is the tenant for the first four buildings on this campus. The registry agrees, naming Oracle as occupant of record on all four, certified the same day.
What the record does not carry for this one. Per building capacity is not separated from the campus total in the sources read. The certified square footage for this building is not public. Energization dates per building are not public.

[[facility-dfw-04-data-center]] DFW-04 Data Center, a data center on the Texas register
Aligned's Plano building, occupied by Lambda. It is the second Aligned and Lambda pairing in this registry, the other being the Caprock campus at Abernathy.
Investment is $700 million. Building area is 425,000 square feet. Site area is 44 acres. Capacity when complete is 72 megawatts. Delivery increment is 9 megawatts. Address is 401 N. Star Road, Plano, Texas. Power is An onsite substation serves the building. Cooling is Aligned air and liquid cooling. Occupant is Lambda, whose cloud platform is integrated into the building.
Lambda appears in this registry twice, here and at the Caprock campus in Hale County. Aligned owns the building in both cases and Lambda is the certified occupant in both. One trade report gives this building a future capacity figure three orders of magnitude above every other account of it. It is not published here. Where sources disagree by that margin the smaller and better corroborated figure is the one carried.
What the record does not carry for this one. The contracted portion Lambda holds is not separated from the building total. Job commitments and abatement terms are not public. Interconnection detail beyond the onsite substation is not public.

[[facility-denton-data-center]] Denton Data Center, a data center on the Texas register
A Core Scientific site north of Dallas, contracted to CoreWeave under a twelve year term before CoreWeave bought the company outright. Its row carries no owner of record at all, which only four rows in this registry do.
Critical IT load once the contracted power is in is 260 megawatts. Additional contracted power in that announcement is 70 megawatts. Additional contracted revenue at this site is $1.2 billion. Capital Core Scientific committed to fund is $104 million. Initial contract term is 12 years. Renewal options is 2 options. Length of each renewal option is 5 years. Occupant of record is Coreweave Compute Acquisition Co V LLC. Operators of record is Core Scientific, Inc. / Coreweave, Inc. Owner of record is None is listed. Location is Denton, Denton County, north of Dallas.
The occupant of record is a numbered acquisition company rather than CoreWeave itself, and CoreWeave appears separately as an operator. Occupant is a position in an exemption filing. It is not a tenant and it is not a brand. An empty owner column is rare here and it is information. Whoever holds the building did not claim that position in the filing, and the registry does not require the reader to be told why.
What the record does not carry for this one. Square footage and acreage are not public. No owner of record is listed, so the landlord is not in the record. What the site draws today, as against what is contracted, is not public. Whether the certification survived the acquisition unchanged is not stated.

[[facility-ecx-aus31-36]] ECX AUS31-36, a data center on the Texas register
An EdgeConneX facility in the Austin market, where the owner, occupant and operator are all the same EdgeConneX entity. The public record on this one is thin.
Market is Austin. Roles is Owner, occupant and operator are all EdgeConneX MCN Austin entities.
EdgeConneX operates a Cedar Creek campus in the Austin market southeast of the city. Whether this certification covers that campus or another site is not established by the sources read, so no capacity or address is published here.
What the record does not carry for this one. Which physical campus this certification covers is not established. Capacity, square footage and address are not public for this identifier. No primary filing or company release names this facility identifier. This entry is deliberately thin and is a candidate for a second research pass.

[[facility-fermi-data-center-1]] Fermi Data Center 1, a data center on the Texas register
One certification carrying eight separate Fermi entities, among them a turbine warehouse, a high voltage warehouse and a mobile generation company. The entity list alone tells you this is a power project with a data center attached rather than the other way round.
Campus area is 5,769 acres. Stated power potential is 11 gigawatts. Stated AI floor area is 18,000,000 square feet. Phase one target is 1.1 gigawatts. Entities filed under this one certification is 8 units. Location is Amarillo, in the Texas Panhandle, next to the Department of Energy Pantex site. Project name is Project Matador. Generation plan is Federal application for 4 reactors using AP1000 technology, with gas and solar. Partner is A lease with the Texas Tech University System.
Reading the entity list is the fastest way to understand this site. A turbine warehouse and a mobile generation entity are not things a colocation landlord files. The nuclear reactors are at federal application stage. Nothing here says any of them is approved or built, and the phase dates are the company's own targets.
What the record does not carry for this one. No reactor is approved and the timeline is the company's own. Which buildings the single certification actually covers is not stated. Water sourcing for the campus is not public. Cooling design is not public.

[[facility-flamingo]] Flamingo, a data center on the Texas register
An Amazon facility certified under an internal codename. Amazon is owner, occupant and operator of record, so the filing discloses no landlord, no developer and no location, and this codename appears in no public reporting.
Owner, occupant and operator of record is Amazon Data Services, Inc. holds 3 roles in the registry. What the name suggests is Flamingo and Pecos Ranch carry the same certification date. The record does not establish whether they are separate physical sites.
Amazon files Texas projects under internal codenames rather than under its own brand. A state licensing filing for a San Antonio building carries the name Lavender Hill, and this registry carries a set of names that appear in no public reporting at all. For these facilities the Comptroller's list is the only public record that they exist.
What the record does not carry for this one. The county and address are not public. Capacity, square footage and acreage are not public. No filing or company release names this facility. This entry is deliberately thin and is a candidate for a county appraisal district pass.

[[facility-fluidstack-abernathy-data-center]] Fluidstack Abernathy Data Center, a data center on the Texas register
A purpose built AI campus at Abernathy, north of Lubbock, developed by TeraWulf with Fluidstack and backed financially by Google. The state certified Anthropic as its qualifying occupant. It is one of two unrelated data center campuses in the same small town.
Critical IT load is 168 megawatts. Gross capacity is 240 megawatts. Site area is 120 acres. TeraWulf ownership of the joint venture is 50.1 percent. TeraWulf invested capital is $450 million. Google lease backstop is $1.3 billion. Location is Abernathy, Hale County, north of Lubbock. Delivery is Expected in the second half of 2026.
The Comptroller certified Anthropic, PBC as qualifying occupant. TeraWulf's own release places an Anthropic lease at a different campus and describes its majority interest in the Abernathy joint venture as sold to Fluidstack. Both statements can be true about different things and this record does not adjudicate between them. Google is the financial anchor rather than a tenant, backstopping the lease obligations so the project could raise debt.
What the record does not carry for this one. Building square footage is not public. Cooling design is not public. Generator count and permit numbers are not public. Interconnection detail is not public.

[[facility-helo1-dc]] HELO1 DC, a data center on the Texas register
A Dickens County site that mined bitcoin under Argo. Galaxy bought it and now leases the whole of it to CoreWeave. Its row is the clearest proof on this site that a registry row names who holds a certification now rather than who held it when it was granted.
Approved campus capacity CoreWeave has committed to lease is 800 megawatts. Critical IT load committed across the first three phases is 526 megawatts. Critical IT load delivered in the first phase is 133 megawatts. Gross power in service for that phase is 200 megawatts. Project financing facility is $1.4 billion. Price Galaxy paid Argo for the site is $65 million. County is Dickens County. Initial lease term is 15 years. Extension options is 2 options. Length of each extension option is 5 years. Occupant of record is CoreWeave. Owner of record is Galaxy Helios I.
The effective date on this row is years before Galaxy bought the site and years before CoreWeave leased it. Nothing is wrong with the row. The state rewrites the parties on a certification while keeping its original date, so a row names the present and dates the past. Every page here is written to that rule. A second Helios certification exists under a later date and names the same occupant. The state spells the first one with a letter where the second uses a digit.
What the record does not carry for this one. Square footage and acreage are not public. Cooling design is not public. The split between retrofit and new build is not public. Which physical buildings each of the two certifications covers is not stated.

[[facility-hutto-data-center-3-llc]] Hutto Data Center 3 LLC, a data center on the Texas register
A second Hutto certification, granted on the same day as the campus row. It names the same occupant. The state files this megasite as more than one certification and does not say where the line between them falls.
Occupant of record is Google LLC. Owners of record is Hutto Data Center 3 LLC / Hutto Data Center Campus Power LLC. Operators of record is Design, LLC / Google LLC. Location is Hutto, Williamson County, northeast of Austin. Effective the same day as is Hutto Data Center Campus LLC.
Two certifications, one date, one occupant. They share a campus power entity between them. A campus certified building by building produces exactly this shape. It is why a count of rows is not a count of buildings and never a count of sites.
What the record does not carry for this one. Capacity, square footage and acreage are not public for this certification. Which building or buildings it covers is not stated. No announcement names this entity.

[[facility-hutto-data-center-campus-llc]] Hutto Data Center Campus LLC, a data center on the Texas register
The certified name is the exact name of the Skybox and Prologis joint venture behind the campus on the Hutto megasite. That venture signed a ten year abatement with the city. The coverage of that agreement named the developers, the acreage and the money. It did not name a tenant. The state record names Google.
Minimum capital investment under the abatement is $10 billion. Site is 159 acres. Planned buildings is 6 buildings. Planned floor area is 3,900,000 square feet. Abatement term is 10 years under Chapter 312. Location is Hutto, Williamson County, northeast of Austin. Frontage is The Hutto megasite, on U.S. 79. Developers is Skybox Datacenters and Prologis. Project name in the developers' own material is PowerCampus Austin. Occupant of record is Google LLC. Owners of record is Hutto Data Center 1 LLC / Hutto Data Center 2 LLC / Hutto Data Center Campus Power LLC. Operators of record is Design, LLC / Google LLC / Hutto Data Center TKD LLC.
The certified name and the abatement counterparty are the same string. That is the whole finding. A reader working from the abatement coverage knows the acreage, the building count and the capital commitment, and does not learn who the buildings are for. This row was rewritten in place two days before this page was written. Google did not appear on it for the first time. It moved from the operator column into the occupant column, Design, LLC moved the other way, and the owner became three entities where it had been one. What the state changed is a role and a party list, not the presence of a name. One of the owners of record is a power entity for the campus rather than a building. Nexus and Hutto both file that way, which is a pattern worth watching wherever a campus generates or steps down its own supply. Design, LLC is on this row and on the Lancaster PowerCampus row, and operates Google facilities at Meitner and at the first of the Bosque parcels. Reading one facility at a time hides it completely.
What the record does not carry for this one. No megawatt figure for this campus is public. Which of the planned buildings this certification covers is not stated. The relationship between this row and the second Hutto certification is not stated in the record. Whether Google occupies the whole campus or part of it is not public.

[[facility-lbb01-data-center]] LBB01 Data Center, a data center on the Texas register
Aligned's Caprock campus, carrying the Lubbock airport code in its name but standing at Abernathy in Hale County. Lambda is the certified occupant. Its cooling is closed loop, which matters here because the campus sits over the Ogallala Aquifer.
Campus capacity is 540 megawatts. Site area is 313 acres. Planned buildings is 6 buildings. Planned campus area is 1,650,000 square feet. Address is 1498 County Road 315, Abernathy, Texas 79311. County is Hale County. Campus building is 1st building at the Caprock campus, named LBB-01. Cooling is Delta cubed air cooling arrays with DeltaFlow liquid cooling capability. Water design is The operator describes a closed loop chilled water system designed to limit water use. Power is Stated as fully renewable by the operator. Service date is LBB-01 slated for the first quarter of 2027.
Abernathy holds two unrelated data center campuses. This one is Aligned's, with Lambda as occupant. The other is the TeraWulf and Fluidstack building with Anthropic as occupant. Nothing in the state record connects them and nothing separates them either. The closed loop design is the operator's own claim about protecting the aquifer beneath the site. It is not a figure this record can verify.
What the record does not carry for this one. Contracted load for Lambda specifically is not public. Investment figures and job commitments are not public. Interconnection and substation detail is not public.

[[facility-lancium-abilene-clean-campus]] Lancium Abilene Clean Campus, a data center on the Texas register
The first certification on the Abilene campus, granted years before the site became the opening address of the Stargate program. Oracle is the occupant of record here and on every other building on this campus.
Certifications the state has granted on this campus is 8 facilities. Secured campus power is 1.2 gigawatts. Combined capital investment announced is $3.4 billion. Crusoe building footprint is 998,000 square feet. Location is Abilene, Taylor County. Occupant of record is Oracle America Cloud Services. Owner of record is Abilene DC 1, LLC.
This campus is eight separate certifications, numbered from the first through the eighth, and Oracle is the occupant of record on all of them. Five were certified on a single day. Reading any one of them alone gives no sense of the size of the thing. The state spells Oracle two ways across this campus and the Vantage buildings, with and without a comma. Counting the strings rather than the company splits the largest occupant in Texas into two smaller ones.
What the record does not carry for this one. Which physical building each of the eight certifications covers is not stated. Water sourcing and cooling design are not public. Per building capacity is not public.

[[facility-lancium-abilene-clean-campus-ii]] Lancium Abilene Clean Campus II, a data center on the Texas register
The Abilene campus that opened the Stargate program. Lancium holds the land and the power, Crusoe built it, and Oracle America Cloud Services is the certified occupant running it for OpenAI workloads.
Crusoe building footprint is 998,000 square feet. Campus land annexed is 800 acres. Parcel leased to Crusoe is 90 acres. Campus substation is 200 megawatts. Combined capital investment is $3.4 billion. Jobs through the initial phase is 100 jobs. Secured campus power is 1.2 gigawatts. Location is Abilene, Taylor County. Announced by is Development Corporation of Abilene, City of Abilene and Taylor County.
The campus is known by three names depending on who is speaking. Lancium calls it the Clean Campus, Crusoe calls it the Abilene campus, and the Stargate program calls it the first site. The announcement did not name the tenant, describing it only by size. The state record later named Oracle America Cloud Services as occupant.
What the record does not carry for this one. Water sourcing and cooling design are not public. Abatement terms and school district agreements were not in the announcement. Street address was not in the announcement.

[[facility-lancium-abilene-clean-campus-iii]] Lancium Abilene Clean Campus III, a data center on the Texas register
The first of the six certifications that took the Abilene campus from two buildings to eight. The state made it effective in the week after the Stargate program was announced and more than a month before the expansion itself was.
Buildings on the campus after the announced expansion is 8 buildings. Buildings on the campus before it is 2 buildings. Campus floor area announced is 4,000,000 square feet. Campus capacity announced is 1.2 gigawatts. Floor area of the first two buildings is 980,000 square feet. Capacity of the first two buildings is 200 megawatts. Workforce announced at peak is 5,000 workers. Owner of record is Abilene DC 3 LLC. Occupant of record is Oracle America Cloud Services. Location is Abilene, Taylor County. Second phase completion announced is Mid 2026.
Two campuses in this record answer to the name Abilene and they are not in the same county. This one is inside Abilene in Taylor County. The Vantage campus runs under an Abilene mailing address from Shackelford County, which is ordinary for a rural site served by a distant post office. Both are occupied by the same Oracle entity, so a reader working from the city line alone would take them for one place. The two state registers do not agree about how much of this campus exists on paper. The Comptroller has certified every building of the announced campus. The construction register carries filings for the first two and none for the rest. It stands alone in the record. Planned critical information technology load for the full campus is 384 megawatts. Planned buildings across the full campus is 8 buildings. Full campus site area is 205 acres. Planned full campus building area is 2,000,000 square feet. First listed building critical load is 144 megawatts. First listed building area is 250,000 square feet. Filed cost for the first two shell buildings is $400 million. Filed area for the first two shell buildings is 760,000 square feet. County agreement site area is 205.756 acres. Filed address is 1395 Bob White Road, Lockhart. Current company campus address is 3300 FM 2720, Lockhart. Filed construction window is June 1st, 2026 through September 30th, 2027. Electric utility named by the developer is Bluebonnet Electric Cooperative with an onsite substation. Cooling design stated by the developer is Closed loop air and liquid cooling. Owner of record is Lockhart Property LLC. Occupant of record is Paile LLC. Operator of record is Lockhart Property LLC. Certification effective is August 17th, 2026.
The county agreement names Lockhart Property as developer and uses Prime's first Austin campus code. That exact company bridge connects the registry entry to Prime's Lockhart campus. Prime's load, acreage, building count and floor area describe the full campus. The registry entry names only the first three numbered facilities, so the full campus figures are not assigned to those facilities alone. The building filing covers the first two shells. Its cost and area do not describe the third facility named in the registry certification. The building filing leaves the tenant field blank while the later registry names Paile as occupant. A blank filing field does not contradict the current registry role. The filed and current company addresses differ. Both are retained because the public sources do not say whether the change reflects an entrance, parcel or address update.
What the record does not carry for this one. The load and building area of the third facility are not public. Delivered power and actual electrical demand are not public. Construction progress and an opening date are not established. The relationship between Paile and any outside computing customer is not public. Expected water use and backup generation are not public.

Second filed construction window is August 6th, 2026 through May 17th, 2028. Third filed construction window is January 5th, 2026 through January 3rd, 2028. City incentive approval is April 8th, 2025. Corporate group bridge is ACS DC Hicks Field Road LLC appears in the ACS consolidated group accounts. Owner of record is ACS DC Hicks Field Road, LLC. Occupant string of record is Google LLC Paile LLC. Operator of record is Vanguard US Serviceco, LLC. Certification effective is August 18th, 2026.
The city agreement and first building filing use the exact registry owner name. That provides the strongest public bridge between the certification and the Fort Worth campus. The later building filings use the same campus name and Hicks Field addresses. One filing names a Vanguard project company as owner. Their figures stay with each building and are not added into a campus total. The registry presents Google LLC Paile LLC as one occupant string. It is preserved exactly because the public registry output does not separate or explain the two company names. The building filings leave tenant fields blank. That does not contradict the newer registry role and does not establish which building an occupant would use. The filed end dates are construction schedules. They do not establish completion, energization or customer acceptance.
What the record does not carry for this one. Planned information technology load and delivered power are not public. The relationship among the registry owner, occupant string and operator is not public. Construction progress and an opening date are not established. Cooling design and expected water use are not public. Backup generation and battery plans are not public.

[[tx-2026-0006]] TRAIGA in force as Business and Commerce Code Chapter 552, enforceable only by the Attorney General
The topic is state policy. The decider is Office of the Attorney General of Texas, a state agency. Its status is decided.
The Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act took effect on January 1st, 2026 as Chapter 552 of the Business and Commerce Code. It bans developing or deploying an AI system with intent to unlawfully discriminate, to manipulate behavior, for social scoring or to produce certain illegal content. It also requires government agencies to tell people when they are interacting with an AI system. The Attorney General has exclusive enforcement authority and the statute creates no private right of action.

The Texas Department of Information Resources published an account on August 14th, 2026 of how it is implementing the artificial intelligence laws passed by the 89th Legislature. Senate Bill 1964, House Bill 3512 and House Bill 149 are named in it. One of them puts an annual artificial intelligence awareness training obligation on certain state and local government employees and officials, and the agency offers a free training video. Another established the state's AI governance framework and directed the agency to develop a public sector sandbox. A third requires governmental entities to disclose their use of AI and creates the Texas Artificial Intelligence Council.
This one is statewide.
August 14th, 2026, takes effect, The agency published its implementation account.
Public access is contact_only. The agency publishes the account and the training video on its own site. The training obligation reaches employees through their own employer rather than through a docket, so there is no hearing and no comment window.

Senate Bill 1964 established the state's AI governance framework and directed the agency to develop a public sector sandbox, quoted as "Senate Bill 1964 established Texas' AI governance framework and directed DIR to develop the Public Sector AI Sandbox and adopt rules for government use of heightened-scrutiny AI.". House Bill 149 requires governmental entities to disclose their use of AI and creates the Texas Artificial Intelligence Council, quoted as "House Bill 149 requires disclosures of use of AI by governmental entities, creating consumer protections, the Texas Artificial Intelligence Council, and a regulatory sandbox while expanding the Information Resources Deployment Review to include agency AI system inventories.".

[[tx-2026-0114]] Grid operator weighs a year's grace for data center cooling equipment on ride-through rules
The topic is power and the grid. The decider is Electric Reliability Council of Texas, a state agency. Its status is pending.
A revision request pending at the Electric Reliability Council of Texas concerns the grid's ride-through requirements. It would give a large computational load up to 365 days after its in-service date to comply. It applies where the cooling load can't meet the standard on the day it starts. The posting names the reason as design and manufacturing limits, including vendors still adapting chiller and variable frequency drive equipment to the applicable standards. Ride-through is the requirement that keeps a large load on the system through a voltage dip rather than dropping off all at once. The request was posted on July 21st, 2026 and is still pending, with the reliability and operations subcommittee named as its next group.
This one is statewide. It sits on the ERCOT grid.
July 21st, 2026, filed, The revision request was posted.
Public access is an open meeting. The grid operator publishes the revision request, its comments and its stage on a public page, and the reliability and operations subcommittee that takes it next meets in public. Comments filed on it are posted beside the request.
The request would allow ride-through compliance up to 365 days after the in-service date where cooling load can't meet it, quoted as "This Nodal Operating Guide Revision Request (NOGRR) permits a Large Computational Load (LCL) to achieve compliance with the applicable ride-through requirements within 365 days after its in-service date where the LCL's cooling load is unable to satisfy such requirements as of the in-service date due to ongoing design and manufacturing limitations, including constraints associated with vendors' continued adaptation of chiller and Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) equipment to the applicable standards.". The request is titled for an extension to cooling load ride-through compliance, quoted as "Extension for LCL Cooling Load Ride-Through Compliance".

system:
You answer questions about the Texas AI Docket, a public record of artificial
intelligence in Texas, from the record given to you below and from nothing else.

WHAT THE RECORD HOLDS. Four things, and a question may want any of them or several at once.
The DECISIONS, which are what a public body decided and when. The DATA CENTERS on the state
register, one dossier each. The CONSTRUCTION the state has registered, totalled by county. And
RESERVOIR STORAGE, by metro and by reservoir. The daily grid and water readings sit above the
index. Somebody asking what is happening in their county is asking about all of it.

WHAT YOU MAY SAY. Only what the record states. Every figure you write must appear in the
record exactly as you write it. Everything you name must be something the record carries. If
the record does not answer the question, say so plainly and say what it does carry instead.
A short true answer beats a long one that reaches.

CITING. Write the id in double square brackets, like [[tx-2026-0001]] for a decision,
[[facility-bexar-1]] for a data center, [[county-dallas]] for a county's construction, and
[[water-lake-travis]] for a reservoir. Never write a bare url.

THE PAGE TURNS THAT INTO A SHORT LINK, either the thing's identifier, like "Docket 59315", or
the source it came from, like "the water record". It is never long.

PUT THE CITATION AFTER WHAT YOU SAY, NOT WHERE THE SUBJECT GOES. Write "No groundwater district
decided that, [[tx-2026-0060]]" and not "The record for [[tx-2026-0060]] doesn't mention it".
Write "Comments close September 4th, 2026, [[tx-2026-0002]]." Write "Two decisions cover it,
[[tx-2026-0003]] and [[tx-2026-0076]]." Say the thing, then cite it.

WHAT YOU MAY NEVER SAY. No verdict on grid reliability. Not a shortfall prediction, not an
all clear, not a blackout call, not a judgement about whether the grid can carry a load. A
unit trip can produce an emergency on a day the numbers looked comfortable, and per site
large load metering is confidential, so that call is not the record's to make. State the
measured figures and stop. The same applies to reservoir storage and to any forecast of what
a decider will decide.

PUNCTUATION. No colons. No semicolons. Write two sentences instead. No em dashes and no en
dashes, and a range reads "X to Y". No emojis. Straight quotes only.

WORDS. Write "can't" and never "cannot". Never open a sentence with "And" or "But". No first
person, so no "I", no "we", no "let me". Dates take the month first with the ordinal, like
"August 11th, 2026", never "11 August" and never a bare "August 11".

THE FIRST PERSON CREEPS BACK IN WHEN YOU DECLINE SOMETHING, and a sentence carrying it is cut
before a reader sees it, so the decline arrives half finished. "I can't help with that" and
"we only track Texas AI decisions" are both stopped. Turning down a question off this record
reads "That is outside what this record covers. It tracks decisions about artificial
intelligence in Texas." Name the record, not yourself.

COMMAS. Keep them sparse. No comma after a coordinating conjunction or a relative pronoun,
and no hedge fenced off by a pair of commas. Write "A data center needs electricity. Most
cooling designs need water too", never "A data center needs electricity and, in most cooling
designs, water". When a sentence needs a comma to hold together, split it into two sentences
instead.

HOW TO SOUND. Like a person who knows the record, talking to someone who asked a fair
question. Not like an assistant. Skip the throat clearing, so no "Great question", no
"Certainly", no "I'd be happy to". Answer first.

WHEN ONE DETAIL IS MISSING, ASK FOR IT AND STOP. Somebody asking whether their county is

WRITE TO THE READER, NOT ABOUT THE RECORD. Say "you" and address them directly. The rule
against first person rules out "I" and "we", and it does NOT mean falling back on the passive
voice, which is what makes an answer read like a machine. "Tell the county and the record can
be checked against it" is the passive doing the work of a pronoun. "Which county are you in?"
is the same question asked by somebody who is actually listening.

Close by offering the one obvious next question, phrased as an offer, like "Want the dates it
moved on?" That offer is loaded into the reader's own field for them, so make it a real
question this record can answer.
